subject: maths
title: Year 10 Maths summary and memory tips

scenes.heading: Year 10 Maths in a nutshell
scenes.sub: Eleven chapters, the rules that matter
scenes.say: This is the whole of Year 10 Maths in a couple of minutes. We will run through the rules you must know, and the memory tricks that make them stick for the exam.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Packing for a trip: only the essentials go in the bag
scenes.science: Revision: keep the key rules and one example for each topic
scenes.breaks: A forgotten item can be bought on holiday. In an exam you must already know the rule, so test yourself before the day.
scenes.say: Revising is like packing for a trip. You cannot take everything, so you pack the essentials: one rule and one example for each topic. The difference is that in an exam you cannot pop out and buy what you forgot, so test yourself first.

scenes.heading: Algebra and lines
points: Same to both sides; flip for a negative
y = mx + c: c is the y-intercept
scenes.say: Algebra first. Do the same to both sides, and flip an inequality when you multiply or divide by a negative. Gradient is rise over run. In y equals m x plus c, c is the y-intercept. Simultaneous equations are solved where two lines cross.

scenes.heading: SOH CAH TOA
notes: Label H, then O, then A
sin = O ÷ H, cos = A ÷ H, tan = O ÷ A
scenes.say: Trigonometry. First draw the right-angled triangle, then mark the angle theta. The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, the opposite side is across from theta, and the adjacent side is next to it. Then SOH CAH TOA tells you which ratio to use.
scenes.caption: Trigonometry: the hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, the opposite side is across from θ, the adjacent side is next to it. Then SOH CAH TOA picks the ratio.

scenes.heading: The quadratic formula
scenes.say: For quadratics, x equals negative b, plus or minus the square root of b squared minus four a c, all over two a. The part under the root is the discriminant: positive means two solutions, zero means one, negative means none.
scenes.caption: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. The discriminant b² − 4ac: positive, two solutions; zero, one; negative, none.

scenes.heading: Reading a parabola
scenes.say: Here is y equals x minus two, squared, minus one. First the U-shaped curve, then its key points. The turning point is two, negative one: inside the bracket, the sign flips. It crosses the x-axis at one and three, and the y-axis at three.
scenes.caption: y = (x − 2)² − 1. The turning point is (2, −1): inside the bracket the sign flips. It crosses the x-axis at 1 and 3, and the y-axis at 3.

scenes.heading: Measurement and chance
points: Cone or pyramid: ⅓ of the prism
scenes.say: Measurement: a cone or pyramid is one third of the matching prism. A sphere has volume four thirds pi r cubed and surface area four pi r squared. In probability, and multiplies, or adds. In a box plot, the interquartile range is the width of the box.
scenes.caption: A cone or pyramid is ⅓ of the matching prism. Sphere: V = (4/3)πr³, SA = 4πr². Probability: AND multiplies, OR adds. Box plot: the IQR is the width of the box.

points: Flip the sign for a negative
SOH CAH TOA; bearings clockwise from N
scenes.say: Quick recap. Flip the inequality for a negative. SOH CAH TOA, and bearings go clockwise from north. The discriminant counts solutions. The angle at the centre is double. And always check by substituting back. Now try the practice questions!
